title: Why Sibling Routes Can't Share State

blocks.content: Why Sibling Routes Can't Share State
Previously, I hinted at a deeper issue. And that is:
EntryDetailPage is a sibling route, rendered by the router at /entries/:id, completely independent of HomePage.
When we navigate from / to /entries/7, HomePage unmounts and its state disappears entirely.
There's no way to share entries between sibling routes using props. There's no shared parent component that holds the state and can hand it to both pages.

blocks.alt: Why Sibling Routes Can't Share State

blocks.content: We need entries to live somewhere both pages can access. That place is context.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
